evals.name: enroll-and-redecide
evals.prompt: A standalone .NET service reads AccountBalance and appends WithdrawalApproved. Another writer can change the balance meanwhile. Explain Chronicle IDecisionReads versus an ordinary passive read, detached enrollment and what to do after a conflict. Do not define an Arc command.
evals.expected_output: Admitted projection fold and guard, Get enrolls in ambient UoW, detached needs explicit enrollment, commit conflict requires reread and redecision.
assertions: Distinguishes a current passive read (fresh but unguarded) from a decision read whose guard validates relevant intervening events at append.
States Get requires ambient unit of work and enrolls it while GetDetached needs explicit AddDecisionRead or guarded append.
Inspects commit success/conflicts and requires a new read and decision on conflict instead of sending stale events without a guard.
States the rule holds only when every writer that decides on it is guarded (or it is a constraint): an unguarded writer can still append on stale state.

evals.name: refused-hierarchy-and-stream-scope
evals.prompt: Our OrderSummary has children. Admit reports Hierarchy. Can we silently read the materialized sink instead? Also explain requirements for a stream-keyed projection decision on one monthly stream at Chronicle 19.50.0.
evals.expected_output: Refusal blocks protected use, redesign only with authority, stream-specific overload with admitted projection and one concrete stream type/id, not reducer or All.
assertions: Explains Hierarchy refuses children/nested projections and does not fall back to an unguarded sink read.
Uses AdmitForStream and stream-scoped Get/GetDetached with event source id, stream type and stream id rather than inventing Arc API.
Requires projections only (not reducers or self-reducing models), one stream type not All, an Id property, and an explicit stream id for stream-keyed models.
Separates no-I/O shape admission from runtime definition, key and fold checks.

evals.name: ownership-and-conflicting-scopes
evals.prompt: Nested code wants to roll back while the owning protected unit of work commits. We also attached an explicit scope to the same source as an enrolled decision read. Can Compatibility policy make this safe? Explain conflicts and an empty checked append.
evals.expected_output: Single owner, Compatibility does not waive protected ownership or completing checks, explicit scope conflicts rejected, empty checked append narrowed to what kernel source supports.
assertions: Requires completion by the owner and does not treat UnitOfWorkIsCompleting as success or permission for nested rollback.
Names DecisionReadConflictsWithConcurrencyScope and incompatible per-source batch scope errors rather than dropping protection.
Explains Compatibility legacy staging applies only to unprotected work; Strict rejects all late staging.

Narrows the empty checked append: current kernel validators accept an empty batch only when a scope has an actual boundary or expects no matching event, an older kernel surfaces DecisionReadValidateOnlyNotSupported, and it must be asserted by an integration specification rather than assumed.

evals.name: cross-key-capacity-and-middleware-commit
evals.prompt: A course holds at most 30 students and a student may take at most 5 courses. Show how to guard both rules in a Chronicle service that commits through the ASP.NET Core unit-of-work middleware, and how the caller learns of a conflict.
evals.expected_output: Two decision reads (course key, student key), one event per event source in one atomic AppendMany, commit before responding via IUnitOfWorkCompletionFeature.CommitAsync, inspect IsSuccess and GetDecisionConflicts.
assertions: Uses one decision read per key and appends one event per event source in a single atomic batch, rather than two separate appends or one read on a single key.
States the middleware commits after the response and reports no concurrency violation, so the handler calls IUnitOfWorkCompletionFeature.CommitAsync() and checks IsSuccess and GetDecisionConflicts().
Requires each decision model to be an event-source-keyed flat projection with an Id property and notes there is no automatic retry on conflict.
Does not present a plain read model, a validator or the default optimistic append as the guard.

evals.name: route-uniqueness-hint-and-hot-key
evals.prompt: We need (a) unique usernames, (b) a 'seats left' badge on the course page and (c) a decision on a key with 200,000 events that is written constantly. Which mechanism does each use, and where would a decision read be the wrong tool?
evals.expected_output: Constraint for (a), plain read for (b), decision read not as the default for (c) because of full-fold cost, with alternatives.
assertions: Routes uniqueness to a Chronicle constraint that binds every writer and states a decision read guards one key's history, not a value across keys.
Routes the badge to a plain read (advisory, may lag) and says it is not enforcement.

Explains a decision read refolds the key's whole history on every read, costs several calls per attempt and is not retried, so a hot long-history key needs shorter histories or accepting an advisory read with reactor repair.
Names what no guard covers: external state, revise/redact and other event sequences.
